title: Where rivers come from and where they go

concepts.label: The Hydrological Cycle
concepts.what: Water evaporates from oceans (502,800 km³/year), most returns as ocean rain; ~9% crosses to land as rain or snow. Rivers are the runoff phase — gravity-driven return to sea. Every river draws on the ocean's evaporative fund.

concepts.label: Global Fresh Water Distribution
concepts.what: 97% of Earth's water is saline. Of 3% fresh: 69% locked in glaciers/ice sheets, ~30% is groundwater, <1% is surface water (rivers + lakes). India's rivers sustain 1 billion+ people from an extraordinarily thin reserve.

concepts.label: Dendritic Drainage Pattern
concepts.what: Tributaries join the main channel at all angles — like branches joining a trunk. Forms on uniformly tilted land with no systematic rock fractures. Most common pattern; dominates the Ganga plains and much of the Indus system.

concepts.label: Trellis Drainage Pattern
concepts.what: Tributaries run parallel to ridges before finding a gap to cross — like a garden trellis. Forms in folded terrain with alternating ridges and valleys. Visible in Himalayan foothills where rivers must cut across the fold system.

concepts.label: Radial Drainage Pattern
concepts.what: Rivers radiate outward from a central dome or cone. Classic example: Amarkantak (Maikal range) — Narmada, Sone, and Mahanadi all begin here and run in completely different directions (west, north, east). A single high point directing three major drainage systems.

concepts.label: Rectangular Drainage Pattern
concepts.what: Rivers make sharp 90° bends where rock is heavily jointed at right angles. Less common. Pattern reveals underlying structural fractures in the rock.

concepts.label: Western Ghats as Master Watershed
concepts.what: The single most important divide in peninsular India. Almost every drop falling east reaches the Bay of Bengal; almost every drop west reaches the Arabian Sea. Controls the direction of all major peninsular rivers.

concepts.label: Aravallis as Indus-Ganga Divide
concepts.what: The Aravallis in the northwest mark the divide between the Indus drainage basin and the Ganga basin. Ancient, heavily eroded range running NE–SW. Geologically older than either river system.

concepts.label: Vindhyas and Satpuras (Narmada–Tapi Director)
concepts.what: East-west ranges across central India hold Narmada and Tapi in rift grabens and direct both rivers westward — while almost all other peninsular rivers drain east. The grabens are structural controls, not just topographic accidents.

concepts.label: Antecedent Rivers (Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra)
concepts.what: The three great Himalayan rivers predate the Himalayas. They were draining the Tethys margins before the mountains rose; as the Indian plate collided and mountains lifted, these rivers kept cutting downward — producing the deep gorges (Indus at Nanga Parbat, Brahmaputra at Namcha Barwa). The mountain is younger than the river.

concepts.label: Indus River System
concepts.what: Rises near Mansarovar Lake (Tibet), enters India through Ladakh. Five major Punjab tributaries: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej — all join before the Indus reaches the sea in Pakistan. Total length ~3,180 km.

concepts.label: Indus Waters Treaty (1960)
concepts.what: World Bank brokered. Three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) allocated to India; three western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan. Partition's hydrological translation — every irrigation canal in Indian Punjab is downstream of this 1960 arithmetic.

concepts.label: Ganga River System (Overview)
concepts.what: Longest river in India at 2,525 km. Begins as Bhagirathi (Gangotri Glacier, Uttarakhand), joined by Alaknanda at Devprayag. Left-bank Himalayan tributaries: Ramganga, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi. Right-bank peninsular tributaries: Chambal, Betwa, Son, Yamuna. ~400 million people in the Ganga basin.

concepts.label: Yamuna (Longest Ganga Tributary)
concepts.what: 1,376 km — longest tributary of the Ganga. Rises at Yamunotri Glacier. Joins Ganga at Prayagraj (Triveni Sangam). Major cities: Delhi, Agra, Mathura along its banks.

concepts.label: Kosi (Sorrow of Bihar)
concepts.what: Left-bank Himalayan tributary of Ganga. Drains much of Nepal. Shifts course by hundreds of kilometres over decades due to massive sediment load and flat plain gradient. One of Asia's most destructive rivers. Called 'Sorrow of Bihar.'

concepts.label: Ganga-Brahmaputra Delta (World's Largest)
concepts.what: World's largest river delta. Ganga splits into distributaries: Hooghly (through Kolkata) and Padma-Meghna system (Bangladesh). Combined delta still actively growing seaward. Houses the Sundarbans mangrove.

concepts.label: Sundarbans (World's Largest Mangrove)
concepts.what: World's largest mangrove forest. Bengal delta — slowly sinking, storm-scoured, saltwater-saturated. UNESCO World Heritage Site. Bengal tiger habitat. Ramsar wetland. Intersection of river, sea, and forest ecology.

concepts.label: Brahmaputra River System
concepts.what: Rises near Mansarovar (Tibet) as Tsangpo; runs east at >4,000 m altitude. Makes near-180° hairpin turn at Namcha Barwa, cuts into Arunachal as Siang, picks up Dibang and Lohit, becomes Brahmaputra in Assam. Braided, sediment-heavy, floods catastrophically nearly every year.

concepts.label: Tsangpo–Siang–Brahmaputra Nomenclature
concepts.what: Same river called different names: Tsangpo (Tibet) → Siang (Arunachal Pradesh, after the gorge) → Brahmaputra (Assam). A single continuous antecedent river with three names across three territories.

concepts.label: Namcha Barwa Gorge
concepts.what: Where the Brahmaputra (Tsangpo) makes its hairpin turn and cuts through the Himalayan front. Deeper than the Grand Canyon. Physical evidence of the antecedent river — cutting downward while the mountains rose around it.

concepts.label: Majuli Island (World's Largest River Island)
concepts.what: World's largest river island in the Brahmaputra, Assam. Product of the river's braided, unstable channel. Shrinking due to ongoing erosion and flooding. Culturally significant for Vaishnavite monasteries (satras).

concepts.label: Himalayan Rivers: Three-Source Perenniality
concepts.what: Himalayan rivers have three simultaneous sources: monsoon rain (Jul–Sep), glacial/snowmelt (Apr–Jun), and year-round groundwater base-flow. Ensures perennial flow even in India's driest months. Fundamental livelihood advantage over peninsular rivers.

concepts.label: Peninsular Rivers: Seasonal Character
concepts.what: No glaciers, no sustained snowfields, smaller catchments, limited groundwater contribution. Many nearly dry in summer. Historical response: tanks (small reservoirs) and dams rather than perennial canal systems. Explains why peninsular irrigation history is different from northern plains.

concepts.label: Mahanadi
concepts.what: Rises in Sihawa hills (Chhattisgarh), drains through Odisha, builds Bay of Bengal delta. Hirakud Dam was one of the longest earthen dams in the world at construction (4.8 km).

concepts.label: Godavari (Dakshin Ganga)
concepts.what: Longest peninsular river. Rises at Trimbakeshwar near Nashik (Maharashtra), crosses full Deccan, reaches Bay of Bengal in Andhra Pradesh. Tributaries: Pranhita, Indravati, Manjira. Called 'Dakshin Ganga.'

concepts.label: Krishna
concepts.what: Rises near Mahabaleshwar (Western Ghats). Major tributaries: Bhima and Tungabhadra. Builds productive delta on Andhra Pradesh coast. Inter-state water dispute between Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh.

concepts.label: Cauvery (and Inter-State Water Dispute)
concepts.what: Rises at Talakaveri, Brahmagiri hills, Coorg (Karnataka). Flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu to coastal delta. Inter-state water dispute predating independence — origins in Mysore princely state vs. Madras Presidency arrangements. Never fully resolved.

concepts.label: Narmada (Westward, Rift Valley)
concepts.what: Rises at Amarkantak, flows westward >1,300 km through rift graben (Vindhyas–Satpuras). Enters Gulf of Khambhat. Narrow graben + steep gradient → no meandering, no delta → builds funnel-shaped estuary instead.

concepts.label: Tapi (Westward, Rift Valley)
concepts.what: Parallel to Narmada, south of Satpuras. Also flows through rift graben westward into Arabian Sea. Same estuary-not-delta character as Narmada for the same structural reason.

concepts.label: Estuary vs. Delta (River Mouth Morphology)
concepts.what: Rift valley rivers (Narmada, Tapi): narrow confined channel, steep gradient, low sediment delivery → funnel-shaped tidal estuary. Open-slope rivers (Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery): long low-gradient journey, sediment-loaded → distributary delta. Synthesis concept owned by ch4 at the river-system scale.

concepts.label: Wular Lake (Largest Freshwater Lake in India)
concepts.what: Largest freshwater lake in India. Kashmir. Occupies a tectonic depression in the Jhelum valley — structural, not glacial. Jhelum flows through it.

concepts.label: Glacial Lakes (Dal, Nainital, Bhimtal)
concepts.what: Dal Lake (Kashmir) and Nainital, Bhimtal (Kumaon hills) are glacial — left by retreating Pleistocene ice. Differ from Wular's tectonic origin. Dal is heavily threatened by eutrophication and encroachment.

concepts.label: Lonar Crater Lake
concepts.what: Saline crater lake in basalt, Maharashtra. Formed by meteorite impact ~50,000 years ago. Only known hypervelocity impact crater in basalt on Earth. Unique geomorphological and chemical environment.

concepts.label: Oxbow Lakes
concepts.what: Cut-off meander loops left behind when a river shortens its course. Common along the Ganga plains where the river has repeatedly shifted. Characteristic feature of mature floodplain rivers.

concepts.label: Sambhar and Didwana (Salt Lakes, Rajasthan)
concepts.what: Salt lakes in Rajasthan — relicts of a more humid past. Salinity is a paleoclimate record of long evaporation cycles and progressive aridification. Sambhar is India's largest inland salt lake and a major salt source.

concepts.label: Chilika Lake (Largest Brackish-Water Lagoon)
concepts.what: Largest brackish-water lagoon in India and one of the largest in Asia. Odisha coast. Ramsar wetland site. Migratory birds from Siberia winter here. Commercially central to coastal Odisha fisheries. Barrier-bar lagoon.

concepts.label: Vembanad Lake (Kerala Backwaters)
concepts.what: Long, narrow backwater system in Kerala — the longest lake in India. Famous for traditional fishing nets and boat races. Ramsar site. Land-water boundary is negotiated rather than drawn.

concepts.label: Pulicat Lagoon
concepts.what: Second-largest brackish-water lagoon in India. Straddles Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border. Barrier-bar lagoon (same formation type as Chilika). Important flamingo habitat.

concepts.label: Bhakra-Nangal Dam
concepts.what: On the Sutlej, Himachal Pradesh. One of the highest concrete gravity dams in the world (226 m). Feeds the Indira Gandhi Canal, irrigating Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan. Called 'temple of resurgent India' by Nehru.

concepts.label: Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC)
concepts.what: Set up 1948, modelled on TVA (USA). First river valley authority in independent India. Damodar was 'Sorrow of Bengal' for catastrophic floods; DVC built for power + irrigation + flood control — the multipurpose template.

concepts.label: Sardar Sarovar Dam (Narmada)
concepts.what: On the Narmada in Gujarat. Completed after decades of legal-political battle. Narmada Bachao Andolan (Medha Patkar) opposed on grounds of tribal displacement (hundreds of thousands). Feeds Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Maharashtra. Landmark in dam/displacement/rights discourse.

concepts.label: Tehri Dam
concepts.what: On the Bhagirathi (upper Ganga), Garhwal Himalaya. Tallest dam in India (~260 m). Built in seismically active zone. Old town of Tehri submerged; inhabitants relocated. Seismic safety concerns remain.

concepts.label: Hirakud Dam
concepts.what: On the Mahanadi, Odisha. One of the longest earthen dams in the world at construction (~4.8 km). First major multipurpose dam project inaugurated in post-independence India (1957). Flood control and irrigation for Odisha.

concepts.label: Johads (Rajasthan Check Dams)
concepts.what: Earthen check dams built by communities in Rajasthan to capture monsoon runoff and recharge groundwater. Community-built, community-maintained. Decayed post-independence with canal expansion. Now being revived as groundwater depletion accelerates in northwest India.

concepts.label: Kuls (Mountain Irrigation Channels)
concepts.what: Irrigation channels in Spiti and Ladakh cut from glacial streams to mountain fields. Allocated turn-by-turn by village custom. High-altitude indigenous water management precisely calibrated to local glacial hydrology.

concepts.label: Zings (Snowmelt Capture, Cold Desert)
concepts.what: Small reservoirs in Ladakh's cold desert capturing snowmelt in areas where no river channel runs. Miniature water storage in a climate where precipitation is locked as snow for months.

concepts.label: Stepwells and Vavs (Gujarat)
concepts.what: Stepped wells in Gujarat and Rajasthan maintaining groundwater access through driest months. Architectural tradition aligned with hydrological function. Rani-ki-Vav (Patan) is UNESCO World Heritage Site.

concepts.label: Tank Irrigation (Peninsular India)
concepts.what: Small human-built reservoirs storing seasonal river flow for irrigation across peninsular India. Historical response to seasonal (non-perennial) rivers. Maintained for centuries; declined with large dam systems. Explains why peninsular South India's agricultural history differs from northern plains.

concepts.label: India's Water Stress (18% population, 4% freshwater)
concepts.what: India has ~18% of world population but only ~4% of fresh water resources. Per-capita availability falling steadily. Groundwater depletion worst in Punjab, Haryana, western UP. Core problem is spatial mismatch — water falls where fewer people are, not absolute shortage.

concepts.label: Ken-Betwa Link (First Inter-Basin Transfer)
concepts.what: Connects Ken river (Madhya Pradesh) to Betwa (Uttar Pradesh) — surplus basin to deficit basin. First inter-basin transfer project under actual construction under National River Linking framework. Ecological objection: Ken flows through Panna Tiger Reserve. Each subsequent link faces harder inter-state negotiations.

asset_assignment_notes.modality_guidance: Drainage patterns (dendritic/trellis/radial/rectangular) → cc-svg (taxonomic diagrams). Water divides and watershed maps → cc-svg (spatial). River system network maps (Ganga tributaries, Brahmaputra course) → cc-svg. Process flows (hydrological cycle, delta formation, meander cutoff → oxbow) → cd-illus or veo-vid. Epic sweeps (antecedent rivers; Brahmaputra hairpin gorge) → cvo-vid (~1/chapter). Topic explainers (Kosi dynamics, DVC/Bhakra story, Narmada Bachao Andolan, traditional water systems) → nlm-vid (~3-5/concept-family). Photographic anchors (Sundarbans, Brahmaputra braided channel from satellite, Chilika, johad, Tehri reservoir) → veo-img. Dynamic transformation (river channel migration, flood pulse, delta growth) → veo-vid (~5-7/chapter).
asset_assignment_notes.rationale: At 3 Veo/day + 1 NLM cinematic/day + 3–5 NLM-vids/day, ch4 should consume ~4–5 days of production. 50 concepts vs. ch3's 58 — slightly leaner, but river system networks and drainage pattern diagrams are cc-svg heavy.
